test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Lemon tastes sour.

options.text: Lemon is sour when it is tasted.
Lemon has been sour when tasted.

solution:
The correct answer is: "**Lemon is sour when it is tasted.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in active voice, with "**Lemon**" as the subject and "**tastes**" as the verb.
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active verb becomes the subject of the passive verb, and the active subject is either omitted or introduced with "by."
 
• To make the sentence passive, we need to say "Lemon is tasted" and add "by someone" or "by people" to indicate who is doing the tasting.
 
• However, the sentence doesn't really make sense in the passive voice, because we don't typically talk about lemons being tasted by someone else. It makes more sense to keep the sentence in the active voice.

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Lemon has been tasted sour**," is grammatically correct but doesn't make sense in this context. It suggests that someone tasted a lemon and found it to be sour, but that doesn't tell us anything about the lemon itself.
 
• "**Lemon is tasted sour**," is grammatically incorrect because it doesn't include a subject for the verb "is tasted."
 
• "**Lemon has been sour when tasted**," is grammatically correct but awkwardly phrased. It suggests that lemons are sometimes sour and sometimes not, depending on when they are tasted.
